old_title: South Africa v Australia: third men's cricket Test, day three - live
new_title: Australia strike late to restrict South Africa to 140-4, just 40 runs ahead, on day three of men's third Test - as it happened
old_text:
It's just brainless cricket from Bedingham. He went out hooking in the first innings after reaching his 50. Here he was set and went out hooking again. I just can't fathom what he was thinking. Clearly he wasn't. One wonders if that's the last we see of him in this Test side, to be honest
WICKET! Bedingham c Lyon b Hazlewood 11 (South Africa 31-2)
What is actually going on?! Bedingham wafts at a short ball with no control, no thought, no appreciation for the game situation or what his team needs, and sends a top edge straight to Lyon down at deep square. Utterly bizarre. South Africa are throwing this series away.
7th over: South Africa 31-1 (Ackerman 15, Bedingham 11) A lot of cricket in this Starc over. It begins with a lovely square drive for four from Bedingham. Then a firmer, more imperious cover drive screams off the bat but it's well fielded. A bumper turns Bedingham into a T-rex as he lifts his hands awkwardly, lucky not to have the ball loop to a fielder. He closes the eventful set with a tuck off his pads for one down to fine leg. Starc runs off the park. He was little a little niggly, but he lopes up the stairs which suggests he's OK.
6th over: South Africa 26-1 (Ackerman 15, Bedingham 6) They're definitely targeting Ackerman with the short ball. There's a catcher under the helmet in place. He swishes at a pull shot but can't get a hold of it. Then he tucks a single off his hips. Bedingham drops into the off side for one before a thick inside edge from Ackerman's prodding blade gets him one down to deep square. Bedingham slices a drive through cover for one. He wanted two but was rightly sent back by his partner.
5th over: South Africa 22-1 (Ackerman 13, Bedingham 4) Starc bangs in a bumper but it almost bounces on his own toes, that's how short it was. It digs into the pitch and comfortabley clears a leaping Carey as it bobbles away for four bonus runs for the Proteas. Super quick, though. He's touching the 150km/h mark. Ackerman does well off the last ball, riding the bounce to tuck a single through square leg.
4th over: South Africa 16-1 (Ackerman 12, Bedingham 3) The Australians placed such a high price on their wickets. The South Africans have not learned any lessons. After Markram gave away his wicket, Ackerman is wafting at a back of a length ball from Hazlewood that rises as it kisses the surface and moves across him. Ackerman scampers a single either side of a pair of ones for Bedingham. This pitch is only going to get harder to bat on, though it still looks decent now. South Africa have to bat for as long as they can to make a game of this.
3rd over: South Africa 13-1 (Ackerman 11, Bedingham 1) Starc has bagged early wickets throughout his career but surely none have come easier than that. Markram will be livid back in the shed as he's put his team in trouble with that soft dismissal. Bedingham, off the mark with a single down to deep point from his first ball, has a proper job to do now.
WICKET! Markram c Head b Starc 1 (South Africa 12-1)
What has Aiden Markram done?! I'll tell you, but if you're South African you won't like it. A full ball, but not a half volley, from Starc is driven firmly but in the air and straight to Head at mid-off. Such a poor shot from such a quality player. That is the frustration with a batter who can look like a dream but haunt your nightmares if you're willing him to produce on a more consistent basis. Starc with a gimme and the Aussies are rolling.
2nd over: South Africa 7-0 (Markram 1, Ackerman 6) Hazlewood is bang on the money from the off, as you'd expect. He beats Ackerman by going across the left hander from over the wicket and then finds the edge from his second ball. But it's played with soft hands flies through a gap between third slip and gully for four. There is a leg slip and Hazlewood bangs it in short and pings Ackerman on the body. The follow up is a gem, beating the outside edge again, squaring him up. He'll keep the strike again with a little flick down to fine leg.
1st over: South Africa 2-0 (Markram 1, Ackerman 1) Starc is finding early movement back into Markram. One is pushed fuller and there's a big appeal for an lbw, but there was clear bat on it. A shorter one allows Markram to stand tall and steer it to a fielder who is already stationed at deep point (I know it's the way of the modern world, but I don't quite get that). Ackerman survives the two balls he has to face, dropping into the covers and running to get off the mark.
Thanks Martin. What a stint from you, and what a game this is! Australia's to lose from here, of course, but anything can happen. The pitch is flat (for now) and is threatening to turn loads on days four and five.
It's hard to walk away from closely watching such a gripping Test. But Daniel Gallan is ready and waiting to take the reins for the rest of day three as South Africa look to knock off their 100-run deficit then ... who knows what will happen from there?!?
Thanks for following along, I'm heading to the sofa to watch the rest of the day's play ...
Australia have compiled a 100-run lead off the back of a second Test century for Josh Inglis (102) and important contributions from Alex Carey (80) and openers Matt Renshaw (74) and Travis Head (41). Cooper Connolly (29) showed promising signs in his second Test as he battled hard for every run while batting with the tail to keep the South African bowlers toiling away. Simon Harmer (4 for 104) was the standout bowler as he made the most of the pitch that looks set to give spinners plenty to work with. Marco Jansen (3 for 60) was below his best today but wrapped up the innings with a fine catch.
Advantage Australia! But surely we've learned to expect more twists in the tale to come with the halfway point of the Test series decider now just minutes away.
WICKET! Connolly c & b Jansen 29 (Australia all out 425)
Connolly finally looks to open up with Australia's No 11 at the crease but mistimes the straight drive and Jansen takes a sharp caught and bowled chance.
125th over: Australia 429-9 (Connolly 29, Hazlewood 4) Mulder finds a way through Lyon's defences to get his reward for a good spell. Hazlewood steps the crease and immediately clobbers a sublime drive through cover for four. The Australia lead reaches 100 runs.
WICKET! Lyon c Harmer b Mulder 1 (Australia 425-9)
Mulder has been troubling Lyon with outswingers since lunch and finally he gets his man. Lyon reaches to prod at a delivery heading for the imaginary fifth stump but can only get an edge to Harmer at second slip who dives low to his right to grasp the chance.
124th over: Australia 425-8 (Connolly 29, Lyon 1) Ooft!Jansen gives Connolly a working over with a short-pitched barrage at varying pace and height. The young Australian keeps his gloves down for a slower bouncer that stays lower than the pitch suggested. But then fails to pick up another bouncer as he ducks and turns his head at the next delivery that fails to get up. The ball crashes into Connolly's helmet and he needs some attention before eventually being allowed to play on. Maiden.
123rd over: Australia 425-8 (Connolly 29, Lyon 1) Mulder has two slips, a gully and the ball moving away from Lyon as the Australian tailender can't help play along. Lyon prods and gets an edge flying towards Harmer in the cordon but the ball bounces just before it reaches the fielder. A fine over and a maiden.
122nd over: Australia 425-8 (Connolly 29, Lyon 1) Jansen picks up the pace with South Africa otherwise offering little threat since lunch. Connolly punishes a half-volley with a blazing drive through cover to the rope. That's one way to keep the scoreboard ticking over while staying on strike. But this time Connolly is unable to find a single late in the over as Jansen ends it with a bouncer.
121st over: Australia 421-8 (Connolly 25, Lyon 1) Connolly works Mulder behind square for a single as Lyon is left with two balls to face. Clever batting from the relatively young Australian.
120th over: Australia 420-8 (Connolly 24, Lyon 1) Jansen keeps staking his claim to be the best cricketer in the family as he holds Australia to a leg-bye.
The Spin newsletter on Marco Jansen has piqued some interest. Though it seems to have overlooked a key ingredient of the Jansen clan.
"Daniel Gallan's otherwise entertaining take on Marco inexplicably failed to mention that the Jansen family lab bioengineered two cricketers, and at the same time. What stars the Jansen parents are!" Stephen Gelb says. "Duan has already played white ball cricket for SA and hopefully one day soon we'll see the two of them playing a test together."
To save you searching too far down the OBO, here is Daniel's story again ...
119th over: Australia 419-8 (Connolly 24, Lyon 1) Mulder takes the ball as South Africa begin with the same pair as in the first session. Connolly drives a half-volley for two through cover and picks up a single as Mulder comes around the wicket and drifts on to his pads. Lyon swings at a ball that darts down the leg side but Mulder is too good to find the bat or keeper's gloves for four byes.
118th over: Australia 412-8 (Connolly 21, Lyon 1) Connolly picks up where he left off before lunch as he keeps Jansen out with South Africa left-arm quick working away back of a length. But Connolly can't resist a shorter ball as he gets under a pull shot and is happy to see it drop safely in a vacant deep backward square. Once again Australia turn down a run as Connolly takes a single to keep the strike.
The players are heading back out on to the Newlands field after lunch. Interesting to note that four of the five Tests since that infamous day in 2018 have been won by the side chasing down their fourth innings target, even if the most recent match at the start of 2025 included South Africa forcing Pakistan to follow on.
Cooper Connolly is on strike as Australia try to build a commanding first innings lead. Marco Jansen has the ball in hand to begin his attempts to do the opposite. Let's play ...
Daniel Gallan will be taking the OBO reins here later today but has earlier opened his mind to the wonder that is Marco Jansen for this week's edition of The Spin newsletter: sign up here.
If you were to bioengineer a cricketer in a laboratory, which attributes would you give them? You would make them tall, with long limbs and a whiplash action to extract steep bounce. Add speed, movement both ways and a left arm to offer a point of difference. With the bat, make sure they can whack sixes but also go down the gears when an innings starts to unravel. For an added trait, have them catch meteorites in the outfield and the cordon.
You might end up with Marco Jansen. At the start of the third Test, the 6ft 8in South African had taken 99 Test wickets at 20.81. His 85 against Australia at Gqeberha in the second Test came after South Africa had slumped to 110 for six before his counterattack helped turn a precarious position into an innings victory. Jansen is still developing as a batter, but his 25.66 average before this current Test understates his potential.
ICYMI, my learned friend Jack Snape scoured David Boon's to-do list as the former Australia top-order batter puts memories of facing the West Indies' bowling cartel behind him to now tackle the equally unenviable task of guiding the big ship that is Cricket Australia.
David Boon walked on to one of the stickier wickets in Australian sport on Wednesday, after Cricket Australia warned the national pastime faces years of financial losses and a period of "cost minimisation". The outlook is grim, and that's without a glance towards a cricketing world of emboldened match-fixers and upturned by Indian interests, facing an Australian summer that is no longer the country's own.
The moustached former Test No 3 batter was sent into the middle due to the ousting of Mike Baird, whose place as chair was pulled out from under him by New South Wales officials unhappy at the manner of his pursuit of BBL private investment.
The runs are flowing once again in the ODI tri-series between England-Sri Lanka-Pakistan, this time with openers Ben Duckett and Tom Banton enjoying the flat deck at Lahore. We hope you don't venture too far away, and not for more than another half hour, but do check in on the white-ball action over at ...
An even session in keeping with much of this series. Australia added 81 runs while South Africa picked up four wickets including Josh Inglis (102) a couple of deliveries after he raised the bat for a century and Alex Carey (80) just as he looked well down the path to also reaching three figures. Simon Harmer claimed those two crucial wickets and he heads to the break with 4 for 104 from 37 overs as the Newlands deck shows signs of favouring the spinners. Cooper Connolly (20 not out) looked solid after a shaky start and was comfortable protecting the strike as Australia look to push their lead past 100 and perhaps well beyond.
116th over: Australia 411-8 (Connolly 20, Lyon 1) Coetzee keeps Connolly on strike as he spends half the over pitching the ball short and the rest sending it out wide. A maiden gives Harmer a shot at Lyon before lunch.
115th over: Australia 411-8 (Connolly 20, Lyon 1) Harmer gets the ball to straighten up and beat Connolly's inside edge. The ball raps him on the pads and the South Africans are up in arms. But the umpire has little interest and Bavuma has even less in considering a review. A single to deep point from the fifth delivery helps keep Connolly on strike.
Cooper Connolly is doing all that he can with the bat at the moment. But he has been underused with the ball in his only two Tests with nine overs in South Africa's first innings in Cape Town, and five overs on debut in Sri Lanka.
"Tuning in inbetween making lowball offers on marketplace - not sure of the logic of dropping one bit-part player in Webster, whose only real crime was to lack much opportunity, for another in Connolly, unless long term hes seen as a viable frontline spin option (which would make room for Boland)," Eamonn Maloney ponders. "What would you pay for a second hand set of bifold doors by the way? This guy's dreamin'."
114th over: Australia 410-8 (Connolly 19, Lyon 1) Connolly turns down an easy single as he is happy to face Coetzee and leave Lyon at the non-striker's end. The South Africa quick overpitches with an attempted yorker and Connolly punches a drive through cover to the rope. He ends the over easing a single to deep point to maintain the strike.
113th over: Australia 405-8 (Connolly 14, Lyon 1) Lyon works the ball off his pads for a single to deep midwicket and Connolly adds another with a drive through cover. Dare I say, Connolly has looked quite comfortable against Harmer.
112th over: Australia 403-8 (Connolly 13, Lyon 1) Coetzee sends Starc on his way and South Africa are just a couple of wickets away from limiting what might have been serious damage to their hopes. Lyon gets off the mark with a glance. Connolly ends the over jabbing out a nasty yorker.
WICKET! Starc c Rickelton b Coetzee 11 (Australia 402-8)
Coetzee gets his first as Starc stands tall and attempts to drive a delivery that pitches back of a length. A thick edge carries through to the keeper just as Starc looked as if he was about to get going.
111th over: Australia 401-7 (Connolly 12, Starc 11) Australia bring up the 400 as Starc clobbers a shorter ball through point and to the rope. He looks for the same stroke off Harmer again but is unable to pick the gap.
110th over: Australia 397-7 (Connolly 12, Starc 7) A better over from Coetzee as he finds his line and varies his length. Starc picks up a single as he steps back, opens the face and prods to deep point. Connolly has been patient but he can't help to end the over taking a swipe at a full and wide delivery.
109th over: Australia 396-7 (Connolly 12, Starc 6) Connolly drives to long-off for a single as Starc picks up the same in less convincing fashion as he guides the ball wide of the cordon.
new_text:
An Inglis century and a flurry of wickets late in the day has Australia in control as South Africa close the third day on 140-4 in their second innings
Here is Geoff Lemon's day three report from the third Test at Newlands ...
If Temba Bavuma was decisive for South Africa as he batted through day after day in Gqeberha, his fall in the shadow of stumps on the third day might prove as decisive at Cape Town. Bowled by a Nathan Lyon classic with eight balls to go, he saw his team reach stumps at 140 for 4, with a lead of just 40 to build on.
Stumps: South Africa 140-4, lead by 40 in their second innings
Another compelling, gripping, dramatic day of Test cricket comes to an end.
Australia well on top thanks to Inglis' ton and some pretty ordinary batting from the South Africans.
Staring at a 100-run defecit, Markram and then Bedingham threw their wickets away before Ackerman was bounced out by Starc for 62.
Bavuma dug in before he was bowled by Lyon playing a rare, and loose, attacking shot late on.
Rickelton, who survived this last over from Starc, the 47th of the innings, will start tomorrow on 8 having picked up two fours alongside Breetzke who was watchful for his 19 off 59 balls.
Batting isn't easy, certainly not on this pitch which is offering great turn, but it's a heck of a lot harder when you gift wickets.
Australia's game to lose, but in this see-sawing series, there is no telling where we'll be this time tomorrow.
46th over: South Africa 131-4 (Breetzke 18, Rickelton 0) Lyon finds Rickelton's outside edge with the first ball to the lefty, pushing off the back foot, but somehow it splits the two slippers and scampers away for four. Oh, what an over from Lyon who compelled the mistake from Bavuma to castle the SA skipper. He almost bagged two in two. South Africa clinging on with mere minutes remaining. They lead by a paltry 35.
Bavuma loses his head and loses his wicket! He's played within himself all innings but this time he swishes at a full ball from Lyon and misses it as it rags out of the rough and knocks him over. Credit to the bowler, who has toiled and tested and challenged for almost 14 overs, but that must go down as another South African who has tamely given his wicket away. I'm not entirely sure where Bavuma was trying to hit that. Lost his shape and he's left the ground with his team in a deep, deep hole.
45th over: South Africa 129-3 (Bavuma 33, Breetzke 18) Starc on for his fourth spell of the day. One more push from the big lefty who has produced some magic moments this Test. He's over the wicket to Breetzke for just a ball before switching to around as he'll look to angle it in and perhaps get it stand up, or shoot through, off the pitch. Breetzke drives away from his body, though he meets it with the full face as he eases it for one down to the sweeper before Bavuma does likewise.
Remarkable speeds from Starc, touching 150km/h even at this late stage. What a warrior he is!
44th over: South Africa 127-3 (Bavuma 32, Breetzke 17) Just the one over for Renshaw as Lyon returns, which makes sense to me. The shadows are lengthening. Such a crucial period in this Test. Bavuma drives twice, which Lyon won't mind, especially as he finds the mid-off fielder on both occasions. A maiden from Gaz.
43rd over: South Africa 127-3 (Bavuma 32, Breetzke 17) Cummins has moved himself a metre off the pitch, standing at a close-in short mid-on. I like it. That means Hazlewood can attack the stumps, which he does after forcing Breetzke to duck under a bouncer. Hazlewood misses his line and offers width and Breetzke eyes it up quickly and eases a lovely square drive to the boundary. Survival is key, but so are runs and the South Africans won't want to miss out on loose stuff. An on drive is hit straight to Cummins to close the over.
42nd over: South Africa 123-3 (Bavuma 32, Breetzke 13) Renshaw replaces Lyon. Again, I don't quite get that. My guess is that the change of pace - he's slower through the air than Lyon - and the fact that Renshaw is a part-timer might cloud the minds of the South Africans. He's also taller, so perhaps a little extra bounce might be found. Bavuma steers into the covers for one but Breetzke is trapped on his crease for three balls. An outside edge squirts past Marnus, who hasn't stopped yapping for a second, and they get another single.
41st over: South Africa 121-3 (Bavuma 31, Breetzke 12) Hazlewood targets the stumps. He almost gets one to burst through Breetzke's defence. A slightly shorter one is met with a firm forward press and they take a cheeky single past the bowler. For Bavuma they move the midwicket to a very wide leg gully, but the short ball doesn't get up and Bavuma tucks it into the newly created gap for one. The bumper to finish the set is down the leg side.
40th over: South Africa 119-3 (Bavuma 30, Breetzke 11) I like this from Lyon, who brings up his cover and tells the Saffas, 'hit me through the field if you want something'. That might compel them to try and hit it harder. It certainly cuts off the easy single. There's an appeal for lbw as Lyon drops on onto the rough and finds Breetzke's pad from his big forward press. Five dot balls come before a stiff push into a gap that allows them to through for a single.
39th over: South Africa 118-3 (Bavuma 30, Breetzke 10) Hazlewood now. He's around that nagging length, looking to bring it back it back into Breetzke off the deck. He then attempts a yorker, or had one slip out his hand. Either way, it gets to Breetzke on the full and os bunted down the ground but there's no run. Dangerous balls, those. Breetzke flicks a single down to fine leg.
Right then. We're a long way away, but what would South Africa want to defend? And what would constitute a 'tricky score', beyond 'something to bowl at'?
38th over: South Africa 117-3 (Bavuma 30, Breetzke 8) Both batters show a bit more intent as they force Lyon off his length by making big strides to meet the ball and negate the spin. Rather than play from the crease, they're able to steer four singles across the over, two down the ground to long on and two through the vacant cover. Better, but hard not to feel like one Lyon delivery will have their name on it.
37th over: South Africa 113-3 (Bavuma 29, Breetzke 7) Even on this pitch, Cummins is able to deliver searing bouncers. For me, he has the best bumper in the game. One cannons off an uncomfortable length and catches Bavuma's glove as the batter looks to protect his head. It could have gone anywhere. Instead ot went over the close leg gully and away for a single.
36th over: South Africa 112-3 (Bavu,a 27, Breetzke 7) Lyon is getting so much turn out of the rough outside off for the right-handers. Bavuma shoulders arms and watches it spit back onto his pads. Lyon appeals. And though it looks totally speculative, it underlines how much it's ragging. Bavuma gets a single away, making room and plinking a cut through cover. South Africa lead by 12 but the crucial thing for them is to not lose another wicket.
35th over: South Africa 111-3 (Bavuma 26, Breetzke 7) Cummins bowls a rare loose ball in this innings, dragging it down to Bavuma who pulls well in front of square for four. Cummins doubles down and then lands a ripper of a bouncer that takes Bavuma by surprise, causing him to hop and duck and pull out of the pull shot. He then works a single past midwicket.
34th over: South Africa 106-3 (Bavuma 21, Breetzke 7) Lyon has Breetzke pinned in his crease, looking pretty ungainly as he does his best to keep gary the Goat out. It's gripping, it's spitting, it's turning. Marnus won't shut up behind the stumps. The fielder at forward short leg is hovering. But he survives the maiden.
33rd over: South Africa 106-3 (Bavuma 21, Breetzke 7) Cummins back on. He's pounding away back of a length before he over pitches slightly and Breetzke sends it back where it came from with a lovely drive for four past the bowler. Cummins brings his length back and finds a little seam. It kept low, and if Breetzke missed that he'd have been plumb. Instead a thick inside edge sees it squirt down to fine leg for one. Cummins to Bavuma and it's a gem, he finds the edge but it doesn't carry! Renshaw, stooping forward, gathers it on the half volley.
32nd over: South Africa 101-3 (Bavuma 21, Breetzke 2) Lyon back. This Australian attack just doesn't let up. Bavuma punches off the back foot to bring up his team's 100 and level the scores. But crucially South Africa have lost three wickets which means they're basically 0-3. That becomes 1-3 when Breetke bat-pads a single past the forward short leg. Bavuma is almost caught in the same area as Lyon is extracting sharp, really sharp, turn. Harmer will like seeing that. The key thing, though, is how many runs will he have to defend?
31st over: South Africa 99-3 (Bavuma 20, Breetzke 1) Starc is peppering Breetzke with some short stuff. When he goes fuller he finds the outside edge, but soft hands means it lands well short of Green at second slip. Bavuma takes a single at the start of the over to close the gap to just one.
30th over: South Africa 98-3 (Bavuma 19, Breetzke 1) Breetzke is off the mark with a clipped single off Connolly. Bavuma takes two of his own. Marnus Labuschagne is whooping and hollering after every ball. He got some stick when he was batting and he's giving it right back. Which is fair enough with his team well on top. At drinks, South Africa still trail by two with their top three back in the hut.
29th over:South Africa 95-3 (Bavuma 17, Breetzke 0) Starc breaks the game open once again after a 64-run stand threatened to swing momentum back towards South Africa. But now the Aussies are firmly back on top. A hayuuuuuuge innings is needed from both these Saffas. Carey and Inglis put on 185 together. Something similar is desperately needed here.
WICKET! Ackerman c Green b Starc 62 (South Africa 95-3)
Starc bounces him out! What a delivery from the left-armer who returns after a change of ends and sends the set batter packing with a ripper! From over the wicket, it keeps going on with the angle, cramping him up as he tries to sway out of the way. A slight edge then a ricochet off the helmet before it looped back towards the cordon where Green make a simple catch. They considered reviewing but missed the deadline, which is just as well as the decision would have stood. South Africa effectively -5 for 3.
28th over: South Africa 95-2 (Ackerman 62, Bavuma 17) Renshaw into the attack. Finger spin from both ends as they look to exploit a perceived weakness from Bavuma, who was dismissed by Renshaw in Durban. The Saffas start by milking him for five comfortable singles to bring the deficit down to just five.
27th over: South Africa 90-2 (Ackerman 59, Bavuma 15) Connolly's left-arm spin joins the part, replacing Hazlewood. Again, I'm surprised by that, but I'm sure Pat Cummins knows a lot more than I do. It's a maiden, though a drag down should have been put away by Bavuma instead of cut straight to backward point.
26th over: South Africa 90-2 (Ackerman 59, Bavuma 15) Starc replaces Lyon, which surprises me. I'd have thought Lyon would bowl out the day as he looked so threatening. Anyway, here comes the big lefty. A full ball invites a drive from Ackerman. He nails it, but Inglis is sharp at cover. Then Starc bumps him and he takes on the pull. It's a thin edge, or a glove, but it's just beyond Carey who can only watch it skip away for four. But that really could have gone anywhere. Ackerman gets another opportunity to drive. He doesn't quite time this one like the last, but finds the gap in front of cover and takes two.
25th over: South Africa 84-2 (Ackerman 53, Bavuma 15) Hazlewood is relentlessly at Bavuma. A bumper is ducked. A back-of-a-length nipper is shoots up and hits the splice of the bat. A tempter outside the off stump is left alone. It's a maiden, with no attacking shots, yet all of cricket was contained in that microverse.
24th over: South Africa 84-2 (Ackerman 53, Bavuma 15) These batters are looking nervy against Lyon. Bavuma rocks back and pulls, but it doesn't quite get up and he just about manages to smear it away for one. Then Ackerman charges - recklessly if you ask me - and smokes it right at short extra. I thought for a second it was a catch but it was hit straight in the ground. Two singles closed the over.
23rd over: South Africa 81-2 (Ackerman 52, Bavuma 13) Really good from Hazlewood who is doing what he does best. Off a great length, a little bit of seam back into Bavuma, he cuts him in half twice, thwacking his body and pad with some delicious movement off the deck. A bit of width allows Bavuma to steer a cut to the sweeper at deep point and that brings up the 50 stand between the two. Their job together has only just begun.
22nd over: South Africa 80-2 (Ackerman 52, Bavuma 12) Ackerman skips down the track, thwacks Lyon through the covers. It's in the air, and as it left the bat every South African in the crowd would have held their breath. Lyon then tempts him with a floater wide of the off stump but Ackerman resists. A single down the ground brings up his 50. Well played Marques. A single from Bavuma brings Ackerman back on strike who goes deep in his crease to cut for two in front of the sweeper at deep point. Phew, another eventful over.
21st over: South Africa 72-2 (Ackerman 45, Bavuma 11) Hazlewood into the attack, replacing Cummins. Two singles to start before he bangs in a bumper to Ackerman from round the wicket. There's a short leg and men in the deep, but he takes on the pull and finds the rope at backward square. Then he dinks a single to deep third. He's playing well, and playing with confidence. Bavuma is brought forward by Hazlewood who finds the edge but it lands short of Marnus at second slip. Oh my goodness, it's so tense!
